headline: Highest risk is data leakage: ChatGPT Desktop can read local files/screenshots while firecrawl has broad network egress and API-key handling, creating a plausible exfiltration path; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are lower but…

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files, screenshots, clipboard, and app context, so malicious web content processed by firecrawl could be copied into it and treated as instructions. firecrawl’s broad scraping/search surfaces make attacker-controlled content plausible. The pair lacks documented provenance tracking, so the interaction is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is pasted or synced into ChatGPT Desktop without provenance labels, injection is plausible.
IF ChatGPT Desktop is used to interpret scraped HTML/markdown as instructions, attacker text can steer behavior.
mitigations: Paste only sanitized excerpts from firecrawl into ChatGPT Desktop.
Add a fixed delimiter and instruction header before any imported content.
Disable clipboard bridging during scraping workflows.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to firecrawl outputs before handoff.

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while firecrawl has broad network egress and handles API keys. If sensitive material from ChatGPT Desktop is forwarded into firecrawl, the pair can exfiltrate it to third-party endpoints. The profiles do not show a shared workspace, so the risk is from operator-mediated transfer plus firecrawl egress.
conditions: IF ChatGPT Desktop content includes secrets, screenshots, or code and is sent to firecrawl, leakage occurs.
IF firecrawl requests or stores API keys while processing imported content, sensitive data may leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Do not send secrets or screenshots from ChatGPT Desktop into firecrawl.
Use redaction before any transfer between agents.
Rotate any API keys used in firecrawl after testing.
Restrict firecrawl jobs to non-sensitive URLs only.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP/redaction on the handoff path.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read local files and app context, and firecrawl can make broad API calls and run as an MCP-compatible client. Even without write access on ChatGPT Desktop, both can act on overlapping external resources and shared inputs, so conflicting updates or duplicated actions are plausible. Uncertainty about the exact orchestration pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same external account or API-backed resource, conflicting writes can occur.
IF firecrawl is used through MCP while ChatGPT Desktop also consumes the same source data, coordination errors are possible.
mitigations: Assign one agent as read-only for shared resources.
Serialize access with a simple manual lock note.
Avoid concurrent runs against the same target account.
requires-engineering: add resource-level locking in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: firecrawl is a crawler/extractor that can produce structured outputs, and ChatGPT Desktop can consume files and app context. If firecrawl’s extracted content is treated as authoritative by ChatGPT Desktop, errors can cascade into downstream reasoning or user-facing outputs. There is no documented verification step between them, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF firecrawl output is used as source-of-truth in ChatGPT Desktop without verification, errors propagate.
IF ChatGPT Desktop summarizes or acts on scraped data from firecrawl, downstream mistakes can multiply.
mitigations: Require a human spot-check of firecrawl outputs before use.
Keep raw scrape output separate from final drafts.
Ask ChatGPT Desktop to cite source URLs for every claim.
Use a second retrieval pass for high-stakes facts.
requires-engineering: add automated validation against source pages.

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while firecrawl handles web content and API keys with broad egress. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch for sensitive data classes, especially if regulated content is scraped or forwarded across vendors. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated data from ChatGPT Desktop is sent to firecrawl, retention/residency obligations may be violated.
IF firecrawl processes EU PII or secrets without a documented DPA or retention policy, compliance gaps emerge.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in cross-agent workflows.
Review vendor retention settings before use.
Keep a written data-class allowlist for both agents.
Delete temporary scrape artifacts after each run.
requires-engineering: obtain and document DPA/residency terms for both services.
